# Independent audit: strict ordinary-depth improvement at a nonvertex fiber



The supplied exact verifier supporting computation verify_nonvertex_strict_ordinary_depth_gain.py completed successfully.

## Anchored-source estimate

The support cancellation is exact for one common integer tilt. A positive weighted average at least \(\rho/2\) guarantees an individual support margin at least \(\rho/2\), without a lower bound on any coefficient. The homothetic copy then contributes the displayed \(\delta\); the positive coefficients are needed for the original Minkowski inclusion and full dimensionality, not for a quantitative coefficient loss.

The separately centered radius-\(R\) containing balls give a uniform section-area bound for every source and every unit continuous normal. The Minkowski body and the ordinary deepest point both lie in the middle body, so their centers have distance at most \(2R\), even when different source fibers are far apart. Consequently the common threshold move loses at most \(2RL\epsilon\le\delta/2\).

In the other normal regime the threshold moves toward the favorable side by more than \(\epsilon\rho/2\) and at most \(r/2\). The middle inball supplies the claimed slab volume. Its section-area estimate is deliberately weaker than the exact ball-section area and is valid in every dimension, including the \(H_0=1\) convention when \(d=1\). The candidate lies in the interior. The two regimes exhaust all nonzero continuous normals and every integer tilt.

For vertical closed caps the entire middle fiber is retained. The inequalities \(A\le|K_w|/2\) and \(G\le|K_w|/2\) verify their budget, with no boundary mass removed.

## Attainment and the vertex dichotomy

Ordinary cap masses are jointly continuous in center and unit normal because every limiting boundary has zero full \(d\)-volume. This gives an attained interior ordinary maximum. A nonvertex has a positive Carathéodory representation using other positive fibers, and its actual Minkowski average is a full-dimensional subset of the middle fiber. All hypotheses of the quantitative lemma are therefore available.

At a vertex, finite strict base exposure allows each ordinary cap to be extended with a sufficiently large finite integer tilt excluding every other positive fiber. This proves pointwise equality of mixed and ordinary depth on that fiber. The upper-semicontinuity argument for the mixed maximum is also correct: fixed-normal closed-cap masses are upper semicontinuous in the candidate, and their infimum remains upper semicontinuous.

## Shape-only constants and examples

At the true centroid, the cap between its level and the support level has mass at least \(\Gamma_d\nu\) and at most its width times \(\omega R^{d-1}\). Thus every support distance is at least \(r_0\), giving the asserted inball. The same applies at an ordinary deepest point. Weighted Minkowski addition preserves the common inball radius, so no coefficient lower bound enters the constants.

The interval family with endpoint heights \(t\) and middle height one has exactly five polygon vertices for \(0<t\le1/3\). Its local-depth formula is indeed \((1+t)/2\). The second rational calibration has the stated constants and actual all-cap depth \(751/300\).

## Limited-cardinality equality classification

The largest-fiber argument forces the stated count and equal volumes. Ordinary simplex rigidity and the new strict nonvertex theorem force the remaining two conditions. The converse follows from the pointwise vertex isolation, for every candidate in every positive fiber.

A zero-volume fiber cannot lie over an integer point of the convex hull of the positive bases: an anchored positive-fiber Minkowski combination would give it positive volume. Its base therefore admits strict separation from that convex hull, and a vertical cap through the zero-volume candidate has zero source mass. Such candidates cannot spoil the classification, even when the original ambient body has additional parts beyond the positive-fiber hull.

The theorem and classification retain their advertised scope. Strictness alone gives no dimension-only gain under collapsing source fibers and no cardinality reduction for sources with more than \(2^n\) positive bases.
